target.title: fix(codex): preserve UTF-16 pairs in tool output delta truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex streaming tool output display renders a corrupted glyph ("�") when a non-BMP character (emoji like 😀) straddles the 8,000-character progress-message truncation boundary. The raw `.slice(0, remainingChars)` on the emitted delta cuts at a UTF-16 code-unit boundary — when `remainingChars` lands on the HIGH surrogate of a surrogate pair, the truncated progress message carries a dangling `\uD83D` that corrupts the rendered output in the chat transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` is already imported on line 29 and used at two other call sites in the same file (lines 3413, 3435) for the 10,000-char transcript-output path. This single progress-message call site at line 1447 was missed during the original import. The fix reuses the canonical helper — no new abstraction, no new import.

## User Impact

Streaming tool output in the Codex chat UI no longer renders a corrupted replacement character when model-generated tool output contains emoji characters near the 8,000-character progress limit. ASCII-only output is unaffected.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A non-BMP character (emoji surrogate pair) that straddles the `TOOL_PROGRESS_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` (8,000) boundary in the Codex event projector's `handleOutputDelta` progress-message path must not produce a lone surrogate in the emitted transcript text.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, x64, linux, OpenClaw checkout at `2d0d06d3f1`

### Evidence after fix

**A. Production module proof** — imports real `truncateUtf16Safe` from `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.js`, simulates the projector's delta loop with the 8,000-char cap:

```
=== POSITIVE (fix: truncateUtf16Safe from production module) ===

module: packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.js
[c1] remaining=1, delta=😀hello (surrogate split)  chars=7999/8000 deltaCount=2
  ok: no lone surrogates
[c2] remaining=2, delta=😀 (exactly fits)  chars=8000/8000
  ok: emoji intact
  ok: no lone surrogates
[c3] remaining=2, delta=x😀y (cut at HIGH surrogate)  chars=7999/8000
  ok: no lone surrogates
  ok: emoji excluded cleanly
[c4] ASCII: remaining=10, delta=10 chars  chars=8000/8000
  ok: chunks clean

=== NEGATIVE (old: .slice(0, remainingChars)) ===

[n1] remaining=1, delta=😀hello  chars=8000/8000
  BUG: lone surrogate U+D83D at [0] "\ud83d"
  ok: bug reproduced (lone surrogate emitted)
[n2] remaining=2, delta=x😀y (cut after HIGH, before LOW)  chars=8000/8000
  BUG: lone surrogate U+D83D at [1] "x\ud83d"
  ok: bug reproduced (lone surrogate emitted)

=== Summary ===
node=v22.22.0 MAX=8000 source=production truncateUtf16Safe
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed
```

**B. Real CodexAppServerEventProjector vitest** — `verboseLevel: "full"` + `onToolResult` spy drives the complete production chain `handleNotification → handleItemStarted → handleOutputDelta → emitToolResultMessage` across the 8,000-char cap with 3 edge cases (remainingChars=1 emoji-split, remainingChars=2 mid-surrogate cut, ASCII-only):

```
✓ keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap 73ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 146 skipped (147)
```

Adjacent UTF-16 tests also pass (no regression):
```
✓ keeps final command output UTF-16 safe at the transcript limit
✓ keeps streamed command output UTF-16 safe at the transcript limit
✓ keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap
✓ freezes streamed raw prefix after UTF-16-safe truncation so full-output echoes stay suppressed

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed | 143 skipped (147)
```

### Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced)

Reverting `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts` to `origin/main` (`.slice(0, remainingChars)`), same vitest test, same environment:

```
=== NEGATIVE CONTROL ===
=== git show origin/main → .slice(0, remainingChars) ===

 ❯ |extension-codex| event-projector.test.ts (147 tests | 1 failed | 146 skipped) 118ms
     × keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap 110ms

 FAIL  |extension-codex| event-projector.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector
   > keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap
AssertionError: expected '🛠️ Bash\n```txt\n�\n...(truncated)..…' not to match
  /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/u

+ Received:
"🛠️ Bash
```txt
�
...(truncated)...
```"

 ❯ event-projector.test.ts:3797:24
    3795|     expect(allTexts.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    3796|     for (const text of allTexts) {
    3797|       expect(text).not.toMatch(LONE_SURROGATE);
       |                        ^

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 146 skipped (147)
```

The real projector's `onToolResult` callback received `"🛠️ Bash\n```txt\n�\n...(truncated)...\n```"` — the `�` at position 18 of the fenced block is the lone HIGH surrogate `U+D83D`. The old `.slice(0, 1)` on delta `"😀hello"` cut after the HIGH surrogate byte, producing a dangling code unit that corrupted the markdown-fenced progress output.

Restoring the fix — same test, same environment — passes cleanly:
```
=== FIX RESTORED ===

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 146 skipped (147)
```

### What was not tested

- **Real Codex app-server process:** The projector is driven through its public `handleNotification` API with manually constructed events, not a live Codex Rust process. The event shapes match the upstream Codex protocol (`item/commandExecution/outputDelta`), but a live session with model-generated emoji output at the exact 8,000-char boundary was not reproduced.
- **macOS / Windows:** Proof was collected on Linux x64 only. The fix is platform-independent (pure string manipulation), so cross-OS variation is not expected.
- **Non-bash tools:** Only `commandExecution` (tool name `"bash"`) was tested. Other tool types (`fileChange`, `mcpToolCall`) share the same `handleOutputDelta` entry point and the same `truncateUtf16Safe` call, so a tool-type-specific regression is not expected.

## Evidence

**Change surface:** 1 file, 1 line — `delta.slice(0, remainingChars)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(delta, remainingChars)` at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts:1447`.

| Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Source | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Tests | 1 | 122 | 0 | +122 |
| **Total** | **2** | **123** | **1** | **+122** |

Test-to-fix ratio: 122:1 test lines per production line changed.

**Regression test:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — new test "keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap" drives the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` with `verboseLevel: "full"` through 3 UTF-16 edge cases at the 8,000-char `TOOL_PROGRESS_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` boundary. Positive and negative controls verified in the same environment (see Real behavior proof above).

**Canonical helper contract:** `truncateUtf16Safe` in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts:44` retains the existing maximum-code-unit semantics but backs off when the truncation boundary falls between a valid HIGH and LOW surrogate. Already used at lines 3413 and 3435 in the same file for the 10,000-char transcript-output path.

**Existing coverage:** Adjacent UTF-16 tests ("keeps final command output UTF-16 safe at the transcript limit", "keeps streamed command output UTF-16 safe at the transcript limit", "freezes streamed raw prefix after UTF-16-safe truncation") all pass — no regression on the 10,000-char transcript path.

**No competing PRs:** `gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open "event-projector AND (utf16 OR surrogate OR truncateUtf16Safe)"` returns no open PRs covering the same call site.
